description: Helps you decide what to publish to make your point of view known, from your topic, your take and the reader you write for. Optional proof points, author background, number of articles and article style shape it. Returns, for each article, a headline and a short first draft with the objection it answers, your proof and a way to test the idea, a promotional post for each, a publishing order and sector notes. Your words are quoted as written and no result, customer or figure is invented. Ask whether written customer approval covers the exact material and intended use.

author_background.description: Optional: your role and why you are credible (for example 'a long career in enterprise sales')

num_articles.description: How many articles to outline, a whole number from 1 to 5. If left out, the series has three articles

proof_points.description: Optional: evidence supporting your take: personal stories, client examples, data or stats, one per line, per semicolon or comma-separated. If not provided, proof points to gather are suggested

publication_approval.description: Optional confirmed written approval for this exact customer name, figures, quote and intended use. Ask before publication. A draft cannot grant customer permission.

target_reader.description: Who should read this, named specifically (for example 'Heads of IT at companies with many branches' rather than 'managers')

topic.description: The topic you want to build authority on

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear.

your_take.description: Your own view on this topic: what you believe that others do not, or your contrarian view

name: thought_leadership_series
title: Thought Leadership Series
